analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: Coreweave beats; European Towers in focus; Datacentres Top of mind; Inwit & TI inline; ITV miss (11 Nov 2026)
key_insights: US trading was choppy after October core CPI rose 0.3% versus 0.2% expected, with broad-based strength across underlying components.
Nvidia fell another ~6% on an independent investigation, NYT reporting and a possible House subpoena. The GS desk sees continued long supply and very little buying support.
Broadcom (+3.8%) and AMD (+0.8%) traded as primary beneficiaries of the Nvidia news. Volumes excluding Nvidia were light, with SPX constituents tracking -15%.

CoreWeave raised guidance as demand and backlog stayed strong, and customer prepayments help fund near-term needs. Management stepped back from issuing unsecured debt at current yields, which keeps neocloud funding concerns in view.
Hyperscaler five-year CDS and bond spreads were largely unchanged. Nebius and Cerebras report on 12 Nov as a further test of backlog quality and financing access.
GS says credit markets will drive AI-related names until CDS spreads and unsecured borrowing costs stabilise or fall meaningfully.
TSMC co-COO Kevin Zhang told the Nikkei Forum that leading-edge chip demand remains 'insatiable' (per Nikkei Asia).

INWIT says AGCOM and other Italian authorities want to speed up resolution of its disputes with Swisscom and Telecom Italia. Their legal powers are unclear, and GIR (Andrew) cautions this does not necessarily improve the odds of a favourable outcome.

Telefónica reportedly wants to renegotiate tower rents with American Tower, per El Confidencial. The annual bill now exceeds €2bn, about 21% of operating profit. GS notes TEF has renegotiated with tower companies before, so it is unclear whether this is new.
GS frames AI capex durability as a financing and power story and favours datacentre operators with secured capital and controlled power.

CoreWeave 4-5 year contracts are pricing at $20-25mn/MW and estimated unlevered IRRs have risen to 20-30%. It expects no further parent-level unsecured debt through 2027, with remaining capex mostly funded through DDTLs.

GS Top of Mind (Gabriela Borges) argues AI spending will hold up but credit quality decides the winners. Hyperscalers are best placed and neoclouds funding long-term commitments with uncertain revenues are more exposed. Wider CoreWeave CDS spreads are read as hedging rather than distress.
SoftBank's $3.73bn write-down shows power constraints limit even well-capitalised players. Multi-year turbine lead times and post-midterm uncertainty can delay capacity.
The desk flags a debate on what happens to the circular finance and backstop arrangements if Jensen Huang no longer leads Nvidia.
INWIT 3Q26 was in line with consensus and 2026 guidance was reiterated. GS expects a modestly positive share-price reaction on the faster dispute resolution.
Telecom Italia 3Q was in line and guidance was reiterated. The FCF miss from working capital phasing should reverse in 4Q, and GS expects focus on strategic questions such as Poste's stake build.

ITV missed and guided below as digital ad revenue slowed. 3Q26 revenue missed consensus by 1%, TV advertising fell 8% versus guidance of about 5%, and 4Q advertising is guided down 5-10% versus GS/consensus at -1.3%/-1.8%.

ITV announced £30mn of temporary 4Q savings and a full-year content budget of about £1.2bn. GS cut FY26/27 adjusted EPS by 2%/9% but sees a limited share-price reaction because the weakness is confined to M&E, whose sale to Sky remains on track for 2H27.

Infineon call: upside to the 2027 margin guide (mid-20s segment margin) and supply, not demand, caps growth. Data-centre revenue should reach about EUR4bn and SiC rises from about 700m to above 1bn. Multi-year supply arrangements exceed EUR10bn in combined revenue volume.
TSMC October sales were NT$586b (+15% MoM, +60% YoY), tracking at 34% of 4Q26 consensus, in line.

GIR stays Neutral on TeamViewer after 3Q26: ARR and revenue missed, SMB is under pressure and Enterprise conversion should slow in 4Q. FY26 ARR growth is cut to about -1% and revenue growth to about -2% YoY pro forma.

Sunrise faces investor questions on net cost savings, debt reduction and 'inorganic options' ahead of a Ziggo spin-off. The short thesis rests on worsening negative cash flow, and bears flag dividend funding uncertainty with net debt/EBITDA possibly near 5x by end of next year.

Vodafone call centred on cost savings: net savings 'well above €200mn', approaching a quarter of the €1bn four-year target. The GS author is more cautious given Germany's underlying performance, and there was no comment on Xavier Niel's influence.

Freenet and TEFD extended their term partnership via a term sheet. FY26 guidance is intact, including the €50m GP/EBITDA negative impact, and a final contract could create upside to Freenet's medium-term guidance.
The October CPI upside, following Waller's overnight comments, likely locks in a 25bps hike in December and one more in 1H27. The 10-year yield rose 10bps to 4.98% and rate-sensitive pockets fell.
GS desk flows: activity was a 5 on a 1-10 scale, asset managers were moderate net sellers on large-cap tech supply, and hedge funds were net sellers (short > long) in tech and macro products.

market_movers.rationale: Stock fell about 5.5-6% on an independent investigation, NYT reporting, a possible House subpoena and lawmaker pressure on China dealings. The desk sees long supply and little defensive buying.
Rose 3.8% and traded as a primary beneficiary of the Nvidia news.
Rose about 0.8% alongside Broadcom as a perceived Nvidia beneficiary.
Beat and raised: Q3 revenue $3.661b versus guide $3.45-3.6b and adjusted operating income $379m versus $200-260m guide. Shares rose about 5-7% after hours.
INWIT 3Q26 in line with guidance reiterated. GS expects a modestly positive share-price reaction on faster dispute resolution.
ITV missed 3Q26 and guided 4Q advertising down 5-10%. GS cut FY26/27 adjusted EPS by 2%/9% but expects a limited share-price reaction.
GIR stays Neutral on TeamViewer after ARR and revenue missed and FY26 ARR growth was cut to about -1%.
Telefónica reportedly wants to renegotiate tower rents on the network it sold to American Tower. GS says it is unclear whether this is new.
SAP upgraded to Overweight by JPMorgan (away from GS).
Auto Trader raised to Buy from Hold by Berenberg (away from GS).

sector_views.rationale: Favours operators with secured capital and controlled power, because AI capex durability depends on financing and power access.
INWIT dispute resolution may speed up but the outcome is uncertain, and Telefónica may seek lower tower rents.
ITV's weak advertising outlook is confined to M&E, which is being sold to Sky.

earnings_insights: CoreWeave Q3 reported revenue $3.661b versus company guide $3.45-3.6b. Q3 reported adjusted operating income $379m versus guide $200-260m. Guidance was raised, per the post-bell desk note.
INWIT 3Q26 reported results in line with consensus and 2026 guidance reiterated.
Telecom Italia 3Q26 reported in line with expectations. Guidance reiterated, and the FCF miss from working capital phasing is expected to reverse in 4Q.
ITV 3Q26 reported revenue missed consensus by 1%. M&E missed consensus by 2%, and Studios matched consensus but missed GS estimates by 3%.
ITV reported TV advertising revenue -8% versus company guidance of about -5%. Reported digital advertising growth was 6% over nine months versus 13% in 1H.
ITV guides 4Q advertising revenue down 5-10% versus GS forecast of -1.3% and consensus of -1.8%, implying FY26 advertising down 2-3%.
GS cut ITV FY26/27 adjusted EPS estimates by 2%/9%, and says consensus 2027 EPS could face double-digit downgrades.
Infineon guided 2027 segment margin to mid-20s and sees data-centre revenue reaching about EUR4bn. Depreciation rises EUR300m to EUR2.2bn.

TeamViewer 3Q26 ARR and revenue missed expectations while EBITDA was broadly in line. GIR cut FY26 ARR growth to about -1% and revenue growth to about -2% YoY pro forma, with FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin at 43.3%.
TSMC October sales NT$586b reported (+15% MoM, +60% YoY), tracking at 34% of 4Q26 consensus. The board approved an NT$9/share cash dividend for 3Q26.

Nvidia investigation, a possible House subpoena and China-related restrictions.

Hotter inflation raises the odds of further Fed hikes and higher yields.
INWIT's growth outlook depends heavily on how the Swisscom and Telecom Italia disputes resolve.

Sunrise's dividend funding and leverage, with net debt/EBITDA possibly near 5x by the end of next year.
vol_and_positioning: The GS desk saw long supply in Nvidia and very little defence given uncertainty.
Market-wide volumes excluding Nvidia were light, with SPX constituents tracking -15%, and floor activity was a 5 on a 1-10 scale.
Asset managers were moderate net sellers driven by large-cap tech supply. Hedge funds were net sellers (short > long) concentrated in tech and macro products.
CoreWeave 5-year CDS was about 1,150bp pre-print with bonds yielding above 15-16%, and the desk is watching the CDS reaction.
Hyperscaler five-year CDS and bond spreads were largely unchanged.
Infineon flow was seen as two-way among hedge funds.
geopolitical: US lawmakers are voicing opinions that could trigger increased restrictions on Nvidia's dealings with China.
A possible House subpoena of Nvidia is being weighed by Republican members.
Post-midterm political uncertainty could delay datacentre power capacity decisions.
Italian authorities (AGCOM and others) are seeking to accelerate resolution of INWIT's disputes with Swisscom and Telecom Italia.
Poste's recent stake build in Telecom Italia is cited as a strategic question for investors.
cross_bank_references: GS cites Palihapitiya's view that operators controlling land, power and buildings will outperform those leasing capacity.
JPMorgan upgraded SAP to Overweight and Berenberg raised Auto Trader to Buy from Hold (both noted as away from GS).

tension_points.bull_case: CoreWeave beat and raised, with contracts at $20-25mn/MW, unlevered IRRs of 20-30% and no more parent-level unsecured debt through 2027. Borges reads wider CDS as hedging, not distress.
tension_points.bear_case: CoreWeave stepped back from unsecured debt at current yields, high-yield AI issuance is slowing, and neoclouds funding long commitments with uncertain revenue are exposed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: CDS spreads and unsecured borrowing costs failing to stabilise or fall, with Nebius and Cerebras results on 12 Nov as the next test.

tension_points.bull_case: Italian authorities want to accelerate resolution of the Swisscom and Telecom Italia disputes, which shortens uncertainty.
tension_points.bear_case: Their legal powers are unclear and faster resolution does not necessarily improve the odds of a favourable outcome.
